response.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS order_share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY order_share DESC NULLS LAST, customer_id ASC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Customers are taken from the Orders table, so only customers with at least one order appear. Each order row is one order, and the total is the count of all Orders rows.
Ties at 10th place are broken by ascending customer_id so the result is deterministic. The request allows any tie-break.
The database is SQLite, inferred from the schema syntax. NULLS LAST requires SQLite 3.30 or later. The CAST to REAL avoids integer division.
At least 10 customers have orders, so LIMIT 10 returns exactly 10 rows.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every customer in the Customers table, including those with no orders. Those customers get an order count of 0 and a share of 0, and the same total-orders denominator applies.
alternatives.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(o.order_id) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS order_share FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY order_share DESC NULLS LAST, c.customer_id ASC LIMIT 10;
